source_text: 1. Cod. 221 a. Cap. XXX. 25. Βραχίονές εῖαι Φαραὼ ἡ κακία ἐν πράξει ἁμαρτίας, καὶ ἐν δόγμασιν ἀσεβείας τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκός· οὓς βραχίονας ὁ Θεὸς συντρίβει ὡς ἀγαθός· ὁ Φαραὼ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστὶ σύμβολον τοῦ ἄρχοντος τῆς ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἁμαρτίας. —Συντρίβει ὁ Κύριος τὸν βραχίονα τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν, ἵνα μὴ δύνωνται ἐπιλαβέσθαι μαχαίρας.
orientation: Origen is beginning his commentary on Ezekiel 30:25, explaining the symbolic meaning of Pharaoh's arms.
pass_a_gloss: The arms of Pharaoh are wickedness in sinful action, and in impious teachings the mind of the flesh; which arms God breaks as good; Pharaoh is a symbol of the devil, the ruler of sin among human beings. The Lord breaks the arm of sinners, so that they may not be able to grasp a sword.

choices.why: Keeps the predicate structure and the glossary term 'arms' for βραχίονες.
Literal rendering preserving the prepositional phrase and the noun 'action' for πρᾶξις.
rejected: evil in the practice of sin
wickedness in the deed of sin

choices.why: Standard literal rendering of the Pauline phrase, kept as a noun phrase.
Preserves the predicate adjective ἀγαθός and the verb 'breaks' for συντρίβει.

choices.term: ὁ Φαραὼ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστὶ σύμβολον τοῦ ἄρχοντος τῆς ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἁμαρτίας
choices.english: Pharaoh is a symbol of the devil, the ruler of sin among human beings
choices.why: Keeps 'symbol' for σύμβολον and the appositional genitive phrase for the devil's role.
rejected: Pharaoh is the devil's symbol of the ruler of sin among men
Pharaoh symbolizes the devil, the ruler of sin in humans

choices.english: so that they may not be able to grasp a sword
choices.why: Literal purpose clause with the infinitive 'to grasp' for ἐπιλαβέσθαι and 'sword' for μαχαίρας.
rejected: so that they cannot take hold of a sword
lest they be able to seize a sword

bible_refs.note: The section heading cites Ezekiel 30:25, and the phrase about breaking the arms of Pharaoh echoes the biblical text.

pass_b_english: The arms of Pharaoh are wickedness in sinful action, and the mind of the flesh in impious teachings. God breaks these arms because He is good. Pharaoh is a symbol of the devil, the ruler of sin among human beings. The Lord breaks the arm of sinners so that they cannot grasp a sword.
